title: BenchX projection
description: How stored results become series (docs/design/benchmark-result-schema.md section 4.3): which results are covered, which fact is the axis, which facts must match as is or normalized, which are ignored, conditions on sibling measurements, and invariants a set of results must pass. A project's identity policy is the projection the store maintains on ingest; any other projection, including the comparison profiles of section 5.5, can be materialized over the same results into series of the same form.
$comment: Rules the server enforces: paths are JSON Pointers into the result, limited to the reported coordinates (project, source, benchmark, coordinates) plus /revision/key and /provenance/subject_tree; exactly one axis applies to each result; the most specific scope wins, then the later rule, then the longest path; a null fact never equals anything; an identity policy's axis is /revision/key; a projection whose axis is not /revision/key or /provenance/subject_tree must match /provenance/subject_tree unless mixed_code is true; any change other than description needs a new identity_schema.

identity_schema.description: Versioned name of the projection. Enters comparison_fingerprint, so series of different projections never mix.

default.description: Role of every reported fact no rule names.

mixed_code.description: True when the projection deliberately puts results of different code at one axis value, such as a trend over time.

estimators.description: Estimators to materialize series for. Used when the projection is maintained as series; a comparison names its own.

invariants.description: Checks a set of results must pass before any comparison under this projection (section 5.5).

scope.description: Results the rule applies to; every member present must match, and an empty scope covers everything. Specificity is the number of members.

oneOf.description: match: equal values share a series. ignore: kept on the result and shown beside the series, never splits it.
The fact a series follows, and how its values are ordered.
Match after normalizing: version-prefix keeps the first depth components (2.39.1 at depth 2 is 2.39); map replaces values by a table, keeping unlisted ones; canonical-uri normalizes a source URI.

condition.description: Keeps only results whose sibling measurement (same attempt_key) satisfies a bound. Conditioning on a state the workload itself drives can bias the series (section 4.3).

missing.description: When the sibling is absent or not success.
